beats.say: That black and white square on a poster is not a picture. It's a web address, written in tiny squares.
Each square is either dark or light. Dark means one, light means zero. Together they spell out letters.
Your camera first looks for three big squares in the corners. They tell it which way is up, and how big the code is.
That is why you can scan from any angle, even upside down. The corners tell the phone how to turn the picture.
Then it straightens the grid, and reads the squares one by one, turning them into ones and zeros.
Those bits spell out text, usually a web address, and your phone opens the link.
Part of the code is extra backup data. So even if it's scratched, dirty or partly covered, it can still be read.
That backup has limits, so cover too much and it fails. The code is only a printed address; your phone opens it.
